/blog/post/bts-building-boops-dms.title: BTS: Building Boops & DMs
/blog/post/bts-building-boops-dms.description: Plan events in seconds, with actually fun event pages. Invite guests on any platform. Easily coordinate via Text Blasts and automatic reminders. Share photos, comments, and more.
h2: Why did Partiful add Boop and DM features?
What was the process for building Boops, and how are people using them?
With DMs launching, does this make Partiful a “social media” app?
p: What our newest features mean for the future of Partiful and IRL connections.

We recently added two new features to the Partiful app — Boops and DMs. We felt like Partiful could help you connect more in real life, by adding new ways for you to connect with each other before or after events.
Ally and Amadou, the design and engineering leads behind Boops and DMs, shared some behind-the-scenes of these new Partiful features.

Amadou: Partiful has always been about IRL interactions. And this has worked so well, but that means a lot of people on Partiful are only connected on Partiful, through a mutual event. And so it was important for us to give you a place in the app to interact, so you can strengthen those IRL connections after an event is over.
The longer-term hope, after you use DMs or Boops, is that they take you back in-person again.
Ally: We see people using DMs in so many ways. From telling the host why you can't go, inviting your friends to a party, or best of all - shooting your shot with someone hot on the guest list.

But the biggest value is reconnecting with someone you met at a party. Social media doesn’t always work best for this. You'll meet someone cool. You follow each other on Instagram, you don't really know each other, you talk about your mutuals, maybe. Two months later, you'll like a story, or leave a single comment on a post.
But you go from real life straight to social media, which can really kill a potential connection. Your chances of linking with them again IRL is low to zero.

Amadou: It all started when I went to a dinner party that was hosted on Partiful for Christmas. There were people there that I had never met before, and I met someone I thought was so cool. We hit it off, and I wanted to hang out after but I realized, “Oh, I forgot to get their contact information.”
For me, it felt weird to jump through hoops of, “Let me hit up the host and then try and get in contact with this person,” and I’m not really active on social media.
It made me wish to see a future with Partiful where I could go to someone who I literally spent time with, and send them a message. I pitched it to the team, and that's where Boops came in first.
Ally: We needed to make sure that people even wanted to interact on Partiful in the first place. If we spent five months working on DMs and nobody used it, that would’ve been a huge waste of time.
So we started with Boops: you go to the app, click on someone’s profile from the guest list, and send them a Boop — a single emoji.

It feels very similar to a poke on Facebook. What was a poke, really? You assigned your own meaning to it. Whether it's flirting, whether it's a hello, whether it’s a first step in connecting with someone, like Amadou said, that he wanted to meet and become friends with at a party.

Amadou: When we were conceptualizing this feature, I tested it with Ami (my girlfriend… and my Gen Z consultant). She liked that Boops allowed her to have a really lightweight interaction with others.
Ally: Initially, we thought about just doing a 👋 and that's all. But emojis are so expressive and we wanted to let you choose. A single Boop can mean so much.
You can send a ☕️ as in “Do you want to get coffee” or “You look really tired right now.” Or the 🥊 is awesome — you can have punch wars back and forth.
Amadou: My favorite is 🪩. Or 🕺. It's really fun to send it to friends before events. It's just a good vibe, essentially.
Ally: One of the hardest parts of this project was naming it. We wanted to be unique. It had to be short and memorable. And I think a long term goal was for it to become a verb.
We thought of other ideas like Sparkle, Tickle, Nudge, Bump… and nothing really felt right.
Amadou: We hadn't seen Boop before on other apps, but it is a common word, and we liked the vibe of it — like you’re gently booping someone on the nose.
Ally: We tested with a small percentage of our user base and people loved it! We've been so excited to see people using it — in the product, and as a verb. And that gave us the go ahead to start DMs.
Amadou: To answer the question bluntly, not “social media.”

It's social though. Partiful, by nature, is social. And Partiful, by nature, is a great utility to help people connect. So “social utility” is probably more right. And DMs are there to help you connect.

When we were building this, we really wanted to make sure that people felt comfortable receiving and sending. When you get a Boop, you only get it one time, and if you don’t Boop them back, it ends there.
There are a lot of safeguards around being able to accept a DM, block someone, or just delete the chat. We wanted to make sure that you feel good about using these features.
Ally: More and more, “social media” has become about unrealistic lifestyles. Partiful cuts all that noise away, and the core use will always be connecting with people in real life.

DMs increase the utility of that. You’re not able to DM someone if you haven’t attended an event together. It's essentially making the interactions you have in-person more seamless. We're not under the impression that you're going to stop using iMessage and just communicate on Partiful. The goal is not to keep people DMing.
We actually would much rather prefer you send a message back and forth and then stop, go to the party, and have a great time.

/blog/post/15-resolutions-for-a-peaceful.title: 15 Resolutions for a Peaceful New Year
/blog/post/15-resolutions-for-a-peaceful.description: Plan events in seconds, with actually fun event pages. Invite guests on any platform. Easily coordinate via Text Blasts and automatic reminders. Share photos, comments, and more.
h1: 15 Resolutions for a Peaceful New Year
p: the Partiful team shares their new year's resolutions 👀

No matter where you stand on resolutions, the new year is a good opportunity to sit down with yourself and ask “what would I like to change?” because complacency is the root of suffering and you are in control of your own destiny 🧘‍♀️💥
We asked the Partiful team what their resolutions are for 2025 and the reasons behind them. Here’s what they said, in no particular order:
Use fewer words: people tend to qualify their statements and it adds unnecessary context
Eat maximum 1 subway footlong per month: they’re not even close to 5 dollars anymore
Consistently get to the office before 11:30AM: early bird gets the worm
Grow a plant from a seed: metaphorically and physically
Go on more serious dates: and figure out what I want out of dating
Stop saying yes to people I don’t want to see: life is too short for surface-level relationships
Have a regular sleep schedule: (this was said by 3 diff team members)
Suck more: do things I suck at at least once a week, like roller blade, guitar, etc… exposure therapy to cure my fear of trying new things
Be more decisive: my gut is normally right and the back-and-forth that happens after is unnecessary
Cook every recipe in a cook book: rather than remaking the same 3 I gravitate towards
Buy fewer things: waiting a few days before buying to better differentiate between what I want from what I need
Overshare less: I value my vulnerability, but not every convo needs a miniature traumadump

Stop caring about toxic ex-friendships: the urge to explain why I ducked out of a friendship rarely goes well. I need to protect my peace and not put any energy into wondering if I should clear the air so there aren't awkward interactions at parties down the road.
Give myself more time in between plans: so I’m not running everywhere in 2025
Plan more of my friend’s birthdays: because it’s stressful for them but easy for me
It looks like the team will be setting healthy boundaries and getting lots of sleep in 2025 💘 Let’s see how long that lasts.
Have a friend’s birthday coming up? You’d better get to planning…

p: Decorations, drinks, and a family dumpling recipe to bring in the new year

Last year, Chinese-American artist Alyssa Yang created a series of event posters for Partiful as part of our community initiative. One of those posters is inspired by Alyssa’s own dumpling parties, and features a warm color palette, Lao Gan Ma chili oil, and many hands chopping and assembling dumplings. With Lunar New Year around the corner, we talked to Alyssa about how she plans to celebrate and got the inside scoop on how to host your very own dumpling making party. Full recipe at the end!
Check out our LNY posters for inspo, including one made by Alyssa herself!

Red decorations are traditional for the new year. Lanterns, candles, twinkle lights, pink carnations, mandarin oranges, sandalwood incense are all a good place to start. You can order these online or hit up your local Chinatown for cheap paper goods.
You’ll need the following stations to efficiently put your friends to work. The full recipe is at the end of this article, but these are the stations you’ll want to prep:
Chopping - cleaver or kitchen knife, cutting board
Wrapping - little bowls of water, baking sheets
Boiling - big pot and a timer
When guests arrive, meet them with a drink. Alyssa recommends Moutai, a fancy Chinese white liquor made from fermented red sorghum and water from the Chishui River.

Once all your guests have arrived, show this dumpling folding tutorial on your TV, or Text Blast the video out in advance to teach your guests how to fold. There are many ways to fold dumplings, but this tutorial is good for beginners. Expert tip: it’s better to under-fill them than to overfill.

The chopping station is mundane yet therapeutic, the boiling station is good for those who are nervous in the kitchen, and the folding station will have the most people involved. You can get creative here and have a contest for most chaotic dumpling design. e.g. empanada-style, micro dumplings, rose-shaped, or mega dumplings 😁
If you’re looking for additional activities to entertain guests before the food comas take them out, consider bringing mahjong, card games, or a lantern crafting station.
Host your own Lunar New Year Party

Ingredients1 lb ground pork0.5 lb shrimp1 egg1 cup napa cabbage, minced finely1 cup shiitake mushroom, minced finely1-2 stalks green onion, sliced finely1 pack of dumpling skins1 tbsp sesame oil (or to taste)1.5 tbsp soy sauce (or to taste)0.5 tbsp ginger, minced finelydash of white peppersdash of sugar
Put on some good music and delegate tasks with friends
Set up large mixing bowl for filling, small dish of water for folding, and a pot or pan to cook
Prep meat: devein shrimp if needed, mince finely and combine with ground pork in a mixing bowl
Add the rest of the ingredients (egg, ginger, soy sauce, white pepper, sugar, napa cabbage, shiitake mushroom, green onion, add sesame oil last)
Mix together, stirring in one direction
Optional: you can take a tiny ball of the mixture and microwave briefly until cooked through to taste flavor. all seasonings and ingredients can be adjusted to taste
Take a dumpling skin, hold in the palm of your hand, add a small spoonful of filling to the center
Dip finger in small dish of water so its just a little wet, and use finger to wet a “dot” in the middle of the edge of dumpling skin furthest from you (this helps seal the dumpling skin)
Alyssa folds dumplings this way but there are many ways to do it, so have fun but make sure its sealed properly so it doesn’t leak when cooking!
Boiled dumplings: bring a medium/large pot of water to boil, put dumplings in, stir to prevent sticking, and cook until dumplings are floating (~6-8 min)

Fried dumplings: heat up oil on the pan, add dumplings in a single layer until golden brown/crispy, then pour in a 1/2 cup of water (this will splatter a bit so shield yourself/be careful), and cover with lid immediately to steam the dumplings until the water cooks off

Finish with a dipping sauce of your liking. Alyssa’s go to is a spoonful of Lao Gan Ma chili oil, dash of sesame oil, dash of sugar, equal parts vinegar:soy sauce, fresh minced garlic and green onion slices.

/blog/post/2024-year-in-review.title: Partiful’s Year in Review 🥳
/blog/post/2024-year-in-review.description: Plan events in seconds, with actually fun event pages. Invite guests on any platform. Easily coordinate via Text Blasts and automatic reminders. Share photos, comments, and more.
p: It’s officially time to bid farewell to 2024 — and what a year it has been. 🪩🕺

🪩 It's time to say goodbye to 2024! What a year it's been. As we reflect on our journey at Partiful, we're feeling nostalgic, proud, and incredibly excited for what's next. Let's dive into a year of bold ideas, chaotic parties, and the moments that made 2024 one for the books.
This year, we doubled down on building tools that make hosting your events smoother, smarter, and more collaborative.

Find-a-Time: Take the guesswork (and 37 back-and-forth texts) out of scheduling. This tool lets hosts offer guests a selection of time slots, and everyone can vote on what works best. When the dust settles, you lock in the winning time and finally get the plans out of the group chat.
Org Profiles: A game-changer for collectives, groups and clubs. These profiles allow organizations to create dedicated Partiful accounts, add multiple admins, and post events right to your profile.
Android App: We brought free event planning to an entirely new audience when we launched our Android app earlier this year. And the best part — we won Google’s App of the Year!

Fun lore: in our team Slack, there’s a channel called #partiful-in-the-news, where we keep track of every article, shoutout, and viral moment featuring Partiful. This year, that channel was busier than ever.

As Partiful continues to grow into the go-to way to host social events, we’ve leaned even further into the wild, unhinged spirit of modern partying. Whether it’s a DJ coffee pop-up or a corporate rave, Partiful supports whatever category-defying chaos you can dream up. We even went viral for letting people send their partners invites to dates, study sessions, and what they’re making for dinner — it’s the kind of energy that could only happen on Partiful.

The undisputed highlight of the year was the Timothée Chalamet Lookalike Competition we hosted in collaboration with creator Anthpo. It spiraled in the best way possible — suddenly, dozens of lookalike contests were popping up on Partiful for Dev Patel, Jeremy Allen White, Paul Mescal, Glen Powell, Jack Schlossberg, the list goes on. Before we knew it, Partiful had somehow become the unofficial home of Hollywood Doppelgänger Olympics.
In true Partiful fashion, when we jokingly tweeted about banning lookalike contests on Partiful, even that ended up in the news.

ICYMI, we launched something new on the community side: The Guest List. It’s our little corner of the internet dedicated to stretching attention spans and sparking better conversations about how we socialize. Think of it as your guide to more thoughtful, intentional, and actually doable hosting.

This year, we covered everything from How to Host Dinner in Your Apartment (because tiny spaces deserve big energy) to a behind-the-scenes look at Why We Built Our New DMs Feature to Why We Need Fuckbois. We’re looking forward to keeping these conversations going in 2025.

As Partiful continues to grow, we have the chance to connect with incredible hosts from all ends of the party spectrum. Our community is the reason Partiful has become more than just an event planning tool — that’s why we’re always looking for ways to spotlight and celebrate the hosts who bring it all to life. Here’s how we brought you into the fold this year:
We launched a “Community Made” tab in our poster selector, making it easy to browse and use designs created by Partiful hosts themselves.
This year, we took community creativity to the streets with a wheatpaste campaign featuring posters designed by our very own community.
We hosted our annual community events, including a yacht party on the Hudson in the summer and our annual holiday party in the winter. We’re a party company, after all 🤷‍♀️

Beyond the big launches, we also rolled out a ton of smaller improvements to make the Partiful experience feel more polished. There are too many improvements to include everything (shoutout our engineering team), but to highlight a few:
Whether it’s a classy dinner or a costume party, you can now pick a font that sets the vibe.
Bullying works, so we gave hosts the ability to remove the “Maybe” option entirely. You can also customize RSVP buttons with different emojis or keep it clean with no emojis at all.

We made it easier than ever to bring someone else on board to manage your event. With our new add co-host link, you can directly invite friends to help plan and manage your party without any complicated permissions or logins.
So, what’s next for Partiful? We’ll be using The Guest List more to keep you in the loop on everything happening behind the scenes, from feature drops to more wild ideas we’re cooking up.

On December 19th, we launched the Partiful After Party, a (highly) requested recap of how you partied this year. Think of it like your very own partying report card — instead of “minutes listened,” you’re getting insights like how many people you invited, what kind of gatherings are your favorite, and how much of a certified party icon you’ve become.
We’d love to see yours! Make sure your app is updated to the latest version to view, then tag us on social… you might just find some exclusive Partiful swag headed your way.
From all of us at Partiful, happy holidays and happy new year! We can’t wait to see how you party in 2025 — and we’ll be right there with you for every unforgettable moment.

/blog/post/new-orleans-inspired-recipes-.description: Plan events in seconds, with actually fun event pages. Invite guests on any platform. Easily coordinate via Text Blasts and automatic reminders. Share photos, comments, and more.
h1: The Big Game in the Big Easy: New Orleans-Inspired Recipes for Your Super Bowl Party
p: Upgrade your snack table to honor the rich culinary stylings of New Orleans

Super Bowl season is upon us and this year it's taking place in one of my favorite cities, New Orleans. The game coincides with the lead-up to Mardi Gras, the city’s busiest and most chaotic time of year. This fusion of festivities feels as serendipitous as a once-in-a-generation celestial event — though it has occurred twice before, in 2013 and 2002.

This February, I am reminded of the horrible disappointment that is the New York Giants and would prefer to tune out the postseason altogether. But if we must come together to watch this marvel of late stage capitalism, we may as well upgrade our snack table to honor the rich culinary stylings of New Orleans, one of America’s greatest food cities.

The king cake is an icon. I can’t say I know why a little plastic naked baby is involved, but it's an aesthetic W in my eyes. For those unfamiliar, hidden inside the king cake lies a small, naked plastic, baby, and whoever finds it in their slice has to throw the next party. They are a little challenging to recreate at home, but if you do opt to bake your own king cake, you can customize it with your team’s colors and opt for hiding a little plastic mascot instead.

Every great food culture has its own take on deep-fried dough, and in New Orleans it's the beignet. Golden, airy pillows of fried perfection, crisp yet impossibly light, dusted with a delicate veil of powdered sugar🤌. You can purchase beignet mix directly from Cafe du Monde with instructions printed right on the box. If you're feeling creative, it would be so cute to try and pipe some royal icing onto the beignets to make them look like little footballs. I would be really impressed if the host of my Super Bowl party did that.
Make a festive 7 layer dip that screams Mardi Gras with purple, green, and gold layers.
Green layers are easy — guac, salsa verde, and a green onion/cilantro/pickled jalapeno topping
Gold layers are full of cheese and optionally, some roasted corn for a textural element

The purple layers are not easy. I suggest using a finely diced red onion for one layer. For a second purple layer I’m cheating a little and adding beet juice to sour cream. A little purple sour cream never hurt anyone
Assemble your layers-- guac, corn, sour cream, salsa verde, red onion, cheese, green toppings and enjoy!

This one is not native to NOLA, but is a must for the halftime purists-or the viewers that go to the bathroom during the plays so they won’t miss the commercials- the casuals. We pay homage to Kendrick Lamar through syrup sandwiches. A syrup sandwich is as simple as maple syrup on bread. If it were me, I would toast the bread, spread a little butter and top with cinnamon sugar. Serve with a side of bananas for the Weezy loyalists.

Canned beer is boring and predictable. Every great party has an experimental signature cocktail that no one knows the ingredients to ✨. Believe it or not, the Voodoo Daiquiri is a local favorite during Mardi Gras season and it's made from just 3 simple ingredients-- 2 parts bourbon, 1 part everclear (!), and 4 parts grape juice. Blend with ice and garnish with a Powerade and Advil on your bedside table.

This last party hack is for the people who really really don’t want to watch a football game. Hijack the Super Bowl watch party and bring all of your friends to the backyard where you’ll spend the February afternoon de-shelling crawfish for tiny morsels of meat,all in the name of paying allegiance to the host city. Not a stretch at all.

/blog/post/bts-playing-cupid.title: BTS: Playing Cupid
/blog/post/bts-playing-cupid.description: An interview with Claire on hosting a party with intention
p: An interview with Claire on hosting a party with intention

On February 8th, Claire, Samira, and Fiona threw the ultimate romantic mixer—sorry, Mixxerrrrr 😘—at Seventh Heaven Bar & Karaoke in Bushwick. 168 guests answered a playful pre-event questionnaire when they RSVP’d, which set the stage for intentional intermingling. I caught up with Claire to get the inside scoop on what went into planning the event, how she pulled it off, and what it’s like to be responsible for 84 potential happily ever afters. 💘
Photos courtusey of @benli.igValerie: So, how were people matched?

Claire: We had a spreadsheet that we pulled from the questionnaire and based off of everybody's responses and the general vibe that they gave, we went through and matched each person with someone we thought they could talk to a lot. We had a success rate of, like, 4%. But, you know, a lot of friends were made and that's all that really matters.
V: When you were doing the pairing, did you feel like a hopeless romantic or a mad scientist?

C: Definitely a mix of both. I think towards the end it was giving mad scientist. There was a lot of data to pass through. We ended up searching for keywords in their responses like “gallery” and pairing people based off of shared interests.
V: What questions did you ask on the questionnaire?
C: We had some general demographic questions, but the main ones were
Describe what you are looking for in your ideal match
What is your ideal date night?
V: Walk me through the event now, people show up— how did they find their match?

C: So originally we wanted to do a more structured approach but it was at a bar and the space was just not really allowing for that. We ended up having a table set up at the beginning with name tags and people put a heart next to their name. If you were single, it would be an empty heart, if you were taken it would be filled in. And then we released the spreadsheet with everyone’s matches an hour before
V: The spreadsheet with everyone’s answers?
C: Yeahhh it was a bit controversial. Samira was like, I don't think we should have done that and then Fiona was like, no, it's fine, no one cares and they're here for a reason.
I guess my stance is, at the end of the day y'all wanted to do this. And if you want to find love you gotta be open to sharing.

C: I also think because of the unstructured-ness it ended up becoming a party where everyone was mingling with everyone. Some people were looking for their matches and they actually met them but for the most part it was just a fun and intimate party. It was snowing out, it was a good vibe.
V: So you said you had a 4% success rate. Can you tell me about this 4%?
C: I had two friends hit me up after asking for the Instagram of the person we matched them with. I think they’re gonna link with them separately
V: What was your biggest challenge while planning this event?
C: I would say the biggest challenge was getting a good ratio of of girls, guys and gays. Making sure that there was a pool for everybody.
V: If you had to describe the party’s energy in one word?
C: Loving. I think because everyone went into the event knowing it was a kind of mixer where you were supposed to talk to people, everybody was just so friendly and open.
V: That's so nice. I love that. I feel like parties should be more open in that way.
C: Yeah, you know, if you're not extroverted it can be hard to just go up to someone random at the bar, but the party’s intention called for that. By the end everyone was singing karaoke together.
V: So what inspired you to host this? Have you done something like this before?

C: No, it was our first time. We have so many single friends it was just a fun little job for us to match people that we know together. We were going back and forth like in theory, these people would be soo good together.
V: Have you always been a matchmaker in your friend groups, or is this a new development?
C: Actually, I set up two friends and they've been in a four year relationship
V: Danggg okay cupid! Are you single or taken?
V: Describe dating in New York City in one word
C: Can I do two words? Choice. Paralysis.
V: Yes. My God. Okay, any final words?

/blog/post/galentines-party-ideas-but-ma.title: Galentine’s Day Ideas, But Make It Chaos
/blog/post/galentines-party-ideas-but-ma.description: Your Galentine's Day party could use some edge. Ditch the clichés for a wild sleepover, feminist horror binge, or a night of manifesting over wine and candle wax.
h1: Galentine’s Day Ideas, But Make It Chaos
h2: Increase your Swag with a Bedazzler
p: Four Party Ideas for the Girlies With a Little Edge

Forget the heart-shaped pancakes and saccharine sentiment—Galentine’s Day is about celebrating your favorite people in a way that feels natural for you and your friends. It should reflect the vibe of the friend group. Whether that means a throwback slumber party, a night of feminist horror, or manifesting your dream life over wine and wax drips, we’ve got ideas to make it happen. Text the group chat, set the vibe, and let’s get into it.

Back in the day, in the pre-smartphone world, we entertained ourselves with our imagination. Tap back into this headspace with your girls this Galentine’s day and throw a slumber party that centers relics from the past. CDs, shitty lip balm, and candy that you would get from your valentine in kindergarden are a great place to start. Decorate your home with paper streamers to solidify the wholesome vibe. No phones unless you’re talking about the iconic plastic makeup compact, or *67-ing your crush.

This one is for the brave gals — a night of iconic women in horror. We’re talking powerhouse performances, eerie transformations, and delicious revenge. From Demi Moore’s gruesome struggle against Hollywood beauty standards in The Substance to Megan Fox’s evisceration of the male gaze in Jennifer’s Body, plus Sissy Spacek’s telekinetic wrath in the face of social alienation in Carrie and Sigourney Weaver’s space-based cat and mouse game in Alien (don’t worry, the cat lives)—this lineup is pure cinematic gold. Grab the popcorn, mix up some themed cocktails, and call it a scary night in.

Sometimes all you need for a party is some paper and pens. If you want to get really crazy, cop these kraft envelopes from muji and candles. Have the girls over to write love letters or manifestos to themselves over some wine. Once all the writing and wine is complete, read them out loud and transform your wine bottles into candle stick holders. Optional, burn the manifestos for some good juju. Pro-tip: write in cursive. What happens at Galentine’s stays at Galentine’s.

Get your guests to bring over everyday objects that they want to add a little sparkle to: lighters, hairbrushes, an old baseball cap, even a bottle of ketchup will do. As the host, you’ll need to buy a bedazzler for the group. These go for less than $20 on amazon or your local craft store. It’s a proven stat that your swag increases with the number of plastic gems you have on you at all times. The bedazzler party is the gift that keeps on giving.
So it’s that time. Pick a party, send the invite, and let the chaos begin.

/blog/post/death-of-the-club-nyc.description: And where you can find your 2025 fix of nostalgia
h1: Remembering NYC’s Graveyard of Closed Clubs
p: And where you can find your 2025 fix of nostalgia

The best part about New York City is that the party always goes on, no matter the host. Bars close, clubs change hands, house parties get shut down — the only thing that doesn't change is New York's appetite for a good time…

While I wasn’t around to document the wild, insanity of New York’s original club staples like CBGB’s, Max’s Kansas City, Studio 54, and the like, I was an NYU student in the late 2010s. And let me tell you, we knew how to party.

Unfortunately for my younger counterparts, most of the beloved clubs I frequented as a naive college student closed during the Covid-19 Pandemic. And with them, it felt like New York’s golden era of clubbing slowly died too.

Today, I’m bringing these relics of the past back into the light for a trip down memory lane. These are the best & brightest NYC clubs that are no more and their modern day equivalents if you’re looking for a taste of 2010s nostalgia.

If you wanted to feel like the hottest bitch around, you went to Up & Down. If you wanted to do drugs with male models in a bathroom stall, you went to Up & Down. If you wanted to get invited to Post Malone’s after party, you went to Up & Down.
Check out: Little Sister Looking for a taste of this iconic 14th st watering hole? Stop by Little Sister for a bouncer that’s as selective and clientele that’s as fabulous.

“Dimes Square” wishes it could be as cool as China Chalet used to be. The famed dim-sum spot also doubled as host to some of the hottest late-night DJ sets ever. This was the go-to for effortlessly chic LES patrons.
Check out: Turks Inn, Sultan RoomYour next best option now that China Chalet is closed forever? The Turks Inn is a Bushwick mainstay with live music in its Sultan Room late-night.

Party goers wanting a no-nonsense great night out knew to grab a cab straight to Williamsburg’s Verboten. With a massive disco ball, a 750 person capacity dancefloor, and arguably the best DJ bill in the city, Verboten was that girl for a reason.
Check out: Mood RingIn lieu of Verboten, Moodring will have you covered for a reliable, always-fabulous good time.

This one goes out to my NYU party girls. Cielo misses you. Its dance floor was a no-rules, reckless abandon that allowed for the most debaucherous under-age nights of my young adulthood, somehow always with a guest appearance by A$AP Ferg.
Check out: Jean'sWant to try to get close to the feeling of being on the Cielo dance floor and still fail? Head to Jeans.

Want to feel like the crème de la crème while being basic as fuck? 1Oak would have been your place. The pros schemed entry to the back room and popped a squat at Leonardo Dicaprio’s strictly under-25 table.
Check out: Zero BondTry Zero Bond for an adrenaline high of celebrity while simultaneously being bored out of your mind.

Travel with me to a place where Moet flows like it’s on tap and Abba reigns supreme. You’ve entered The Jane Hotel Ballroom. Frat flicking on luxury couches in the light of a dim fireplace never felt so good.
Check out: GospelNo establishment will ever compare to the Jane, but you can try Gospel if you’re cool with swapping out ABBA for Afro-House beats while a man in a fedora hits on you.
Interns today will never respect nor understand BBar. Think happy hour meets college bar meets NYC outdoor drinking with an open air ceiling. Yeah. You would have waited in a two block long line too.
Check out: FiddlesticksLooking for the next best finance-bro circle jerk? Try Fiddlesticks in the West Village.

Guys, where did all the classy hookah bars go? Kidding. While Le Souk may have been an embarrassment to night-life establishments everywhere, I will give it this — it was probably the only place in New York you could find statement necklaces, hookah, and French Montana all at the same table.
Check out: Studio 151Vinyl bar Studio 151 will feel like a welcomed upgrade from Le Souk, with its lounge furniture and absence of hookah-related paraphernalia.

Looking to forgo the Manhattan club scene and listen to an actually competent DJ? R.I.P. You would have loved Output. With a massive dance-floor and impressive roof-top for warm summer nights, Output was the go-to for house & techno sets that lasted until the early morning.
Check out: ElsewhereHosting an equally idyllic rooftop and huge main-stage area, Elsewhere has everything you need for a good time akin to those at Output.

My first night at NYU, I followed a mob of under-age students to a greasy underground bar by the name of 13th step. While I tried to avoid it the rest of my college experience, this bar was a beacon that called to me and would not let me go.
Check out: Spring LoungeIn my adulthood, Spring Lounge calls me to me in much the same way. Unfortunately.

h3: What are cookies and similar technologies?
What types of cookies do we use?
How often will we update this cookie policy?
Where can you get further information?
p: This Cookie Policy explains how Partiful, Co. (“we,” “us,” or “our”) uses cookies and similar technologies. It explains what these technologies are and why we use them, as well as your rights to control our use of them.

This Cookie Policy should be read in conjunction with our Privacy Policy. If you have any questions or concerns about the Cookie Policy or its implementation, please contact us at hello@partiful.com, or as otherwise described in our Privacy Policy.

‍Cookies. A cookie is a text file containing a string of characters that is sent to your device when you visit a website. When you visit the site again, the cookie allows that site to recognize your browser. Cookies may store user preferences and other information. Cookies set by the website owner (in this case, Partiful) are called "first party cookies." Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third party cookies”. Third party cookies enable third party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website (e.g. advertising, interactive content, and analytics). The parties that set these third party cookies can recognize your computer both when it visits the website in question and also when it visits certain other websites.

Local storage. Local storage technologies refer to the methods that web applications use to store data locally on your device. The most commonly used local storage technology is called "localStorage" and is part of the HTML5 standard. This technology allows web applications to store data that persists even after the user closes their browser or restarts their device.

Session storage. Session storage is a feature of your web browser that allows a website to temporarily store data on your device while you are actively using the website. This data is deleted as soon as you close your browser or navigate away from the website. Websites may use session storage to improve your experience and ensure that certain information is readily available during your browsing session.

Other tracking technologies. Websites and emails contain a variety of tracking technologies, including web beacons (also known as tracking pixels), third-party tracking scripts, advertising pixels, and analytics tools. These technologies provide data on how individuals interact with emails websites and allow websites to serve personalized advertisements.
This Cookie Policy refers to all these technologies collectively as “cookies.”

We use cookies for several reasons. Some cookies are required for technical reasons in order for our website to operate, and we refer to these as "strictly necessary" cookies. Other cookies also enable us to track and target the interests of our users to enhance the experience on our website and services more broadly. For example, our cookies may help to distinguish you from other users of our services for the purposes of helping you navigate between pages efficiently, remembering your preferences, enabling functionality, helping us understand activity and patterns, and facilitating online advertising.
Third parties set cookies on our website for analytics, and other purposes. This is described in more detail below.
We and our service providers automatically log information about an individual’s interactions with our website and services, such as:

Online activity information, such as pages or screens viewed, how long individuals spend on a page or screen, the website they visited before browsing to our website, navigation paths between pages or screens, information about activity on a page or screen, access times and duration of access, and whether individuals open our marketing emails or click links within them.

Device information, such as computer or mobile device operating system type and version, manufacturer and model, browser type, screen resolution, RAM and disk size, CPU usage, device type (e.g., phone, tablet), IP address, unique identifiers (including identifiers used for advertising purposes), language settings, mobile device carrier, radio/network information (e.g., WiFi, LTE,5G), and general location information such as city, state, or geographic area.

We use both persistent cookies and session cookies.Persistent cookies stay on your device for a set period of time or until you delete them, while session cookies are deleted once you close your web browser.We use persistent cookies, for example, to remember any preferences you have or choices you make when you use our website.
In this section, we outline the specific types of cookies served through our website and the purposes they serve.These cookies include:

Strictly necessary cookies: These cookies are strictly necessary to provide you with services available through our website. They provide page navigation functionality and access to secure areas. You can set your browser to block these cookies, but then some parts of the services will not work.

Performance cookies: These cookies are used to enhance the performance and functionality of our website but are not essential for its use. However, without these cookies, certain functionality may become unavailable.

Functional cookies: These cookies enhance the performance of our website(e.g., they allow us to remember your preferences and settings). Without these cookies, certain functionality may become unavailable.

·Analytics cookies. These cookies help us understand how you interact with our websites by providing information such as the pages visited, the time spent on the websites, and any issues encountered, such as error messages. The information these cookies collect are for the purposes of generating aggregated statistics and they help us improve the way our websites work. Where required by law, we will obtain your consent before placing Analytics Cookies on your device.

Advertising/targeting cookies: We and our third-party advertising partners use these cookies to collect information about how you use our website and use that information to serve online ads that may be relevant to your interests. They perform functions like preventing the same ad from continuously reappearing, ensuring that ads are properly displayed for advertisers, and in some cases selecting advertisements that are based on your interests.
You can limit online tracking by:

Blocking cookies in your browser. Most browsers let you remove or reject cookies. To do this, follow the instructions in your browser settings.Many browsers accept cookies by default until you change your settings. For more information about cookies, including how to see what cookies have been set on your device and how to manage and delete them, visit www.allaboutcookies.org. Use the following links to learn more about how to control cookies and online tracking through your browser:

Using privacy plug-ins or browsers. You can block our website from setting cookies used for interest-based ads by using a browser with privacy features, like Brave, or installing browser plugins like Privacy Badger, Ghostery, or uBlock Origin, and configuring them to block third party cookies/trackers.

Note that because these opt-out mechanisms are specific to the device or browser on which they are exercised, you will need to opt out on each browser and device that you use. Do Not Track. Some Internet browsers can be configured to send “Do Not Track” signals to the online services that you visit. We currently do not respond to “Do Not Track” or similar signals. To find out more about “Do Not Track,” please visit  http://www.allaboutdnt.com.

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time in order to reflect, for example, changes to the cookies we use or for other operational, legal or regulatory reasons. We will notify you of any material changes to this Cookie Policy prior to the changes becoming effective by posting the changes on this page and providing a more prominent notice with on-site or email notifications. Please therefore re-visit this Cookie Policy regularly to stay informed about our use of cookies and related technologies.
The date at the top of this Cookie Policy indicates when it was last updated.
If you have any questions about our use of cookies, please email us at hello@partiful.com.

h1: Best Platform to Sell Halloween Party Tickets: What to Look For in 2026
h2: 2. Whether guests can see who else is coming
3. Whether you need reserved seating or a box office
6. Whether the platform helps anyone find your party
h3: Can I sell tickets to a house party?
Is Partiful better than Eventbrite for parties?
What should I look for in a ticketing platform for a party?
Do I need a separate app for check-in?
p: The six things that actually matter when picking a ticketing platform for a Halloween party: how invites travel, check-in, payout timing, and when a party platform beats a box office.

The right ticketing platform for a Halloween party depends on one question: does your party fill up because people saw a friend going, or because strangers found a listing? If it’s the former, a house party, a warehouse party, a supper club, a collective’s annual night, you want a platform built around a social event page, where the ticket sits next to a visible guest list and spreads through group chats. If it’s the latter, or if you need reserved seating or a box office, you want a dedicated ticketing platform. Here are the six criteria that decide it.
Halloween 2026 falls on a Saturday, which means peak demand and peak competition for the same night. Whichever way you go, get tickets live by early October.

This is the criterion most people skip and then regret. Email-first platforms assume you have a mailing list. For a Halloween party, you have group chats. A link dropped in a group chat gets opened; an email gets archived unread. If your distribution is text and Instagram, a platform built around email campaigns is fighting you.

The most powerful thing on a ticketed party page isn’t the flyer: it’s the names. Standard ticketing flow is a checkout form: you buy, then find out who’s coming. That’s backwards for a social party. When guests can see the list filling up, fence-sitters commit, people forward the link to friends who’ll be there, and the party starts feeling inevitable. An empty guest list is the single biggest conversion killer in party ticketing.

If you need assigned seats, timed entry sessions, season passes, box office mode, or offline scanning for a venue with no signal, you need a dedicated ticketing platform. Party-first platforms generally don’t do these, and no amount of good design substitutes.

Every serious platform does QR check-in from a phone now. The differences are in the details: can more than one person scan at once; can a non-host scan; can you check someone in manually; and does it work offline? Partiful doesn’t currently support offline scanning, worth knowing before you book a venue with no reception.

Most platforms pay out after the event, not as tickets sell. Partiful sends payouts roughly three days after your event ends via Stripe. Eventbrite is similar, and additionally holds a 20% reserve until after the event, with first-time paid-event organizers unable to access early payouts at all.

Two different mechanisms, and they suit different events. Listing-driven discovery puts your event in a browsable directory where strangers can find it. Network-driven discovery spreads your event through the friend graph: guests see it because someone they know is going. Partiful works this way, plus local discovery through Explore.
Ask: can I send this by text? Can guests forward it without the recipient needing an account? Does the link preview look like an invitation or like a receipt?
If your party grows by word of mouth, this criterion matters more than anything else.

Eventbrite is the obvious option here. /blog/post/worlds-largest-fitnessgram-pa.title: 1000 People Did the World’s Largest FitnessGram Pacer Test in NYC
/blog/post/worlds-largest-fitnessgram-pa.description: Around 1,000 people gathered in Sheep Meadow for Jordan Haber’s 2026 FitnessGram Pacer Test attempt in Central Park.
h1: 1000 People Did the World’s Largest FitnessGram Pacer Test in NYC
Central Park Took On the World’s Largest FitnessGram Pacer Test (Again)
h2: A record attempt with real structure
From 250 people last year to around 1,000 this year
Next up: Walk the Length of Manhattan
p: Around 1,000 runners gathered in Sheep Meadow for a tightly run, very nostalgic Pacer Test attempt.

At 11 a.m., Sheep Meadow in Central Park filled with runners, spectators, and more than a little gym-class nostalgia after a viral Partiful on the Explore page brought around 1,000 people out for another attempt at the world’s largest FitnessGram Pacer Test, hosted by Jordan Haber — a major step up from last year’s edition, which drew 250 attendees.

The event went viral before runners even reached Sheep Meadow. As of today, 2,079 people had marked themselves as going, 2,308 as interested, and another 450 as maybe — a turnout signal that made the scale of the attempt feel real well before the first whistle.

A few months before the event, Haber posted it to Partiful Explore, where it accumulated thousands of RSVPs naturally. For hosts, Explore can be a way to put a public event in front of people already looking for plans — learn how to get your event featured.

For an event built around the most infamous audio track in school fitness history, the whole thing was remarkably orderly. Participants lined up across the meadow, referees directed the action with whistles, and cones clearly marked the race distance. By the time the test began at about 11:20 a.m., the field had turned into a disciplined, very large relay of runners crossing the line and turning back on cue.

The actual race lasted far longer than most people’s grade-school memories. The eventual winners kept going for about ten whole minutes as the beeps tightened and the pace accelerated. At that point, staying in it was less about remembering the test and more about finding a reason to take one more turn.

The finish came with a medal ceremony celebrating the top three winners, plus the top female finisher. It was a fittingly earnest ending for an event that began as a viral, tongue-in-cheek challenge and became a fully organized Central Park spectacle.

Jordan Haber first brought the Pacer Test to Central Park last year, when 250 people attended. The New York Post covered that original attempt. This year’s turnout made it clear that the joke has grown into a real tradition — one built around a shared childhood reference, a lot of friendly competitiveness, and the rare joy of doing something difficult together in public.

Haber is planning more events, starting with Walk the Length of Manhattan on August 22. Everyone who completes the walk gets a good time, with an after-party location still to be announced. Consider it a different kind of endurance test — fewer beeps, more blocks.

p: Supper clubs are having a moment — intimate, ticketed dinners where strangers become regulars and the table is the whole point. They’re also one of the easiest events to start: you don’t need a restaurant, a liquor license, or a marketing budget. You need a menu, a room, a price, and a way to sell the seats. Here’s how to do all of it, step by step.

A supper club is a ticketed, often recurring dinner hosted in a home, studio, or borrowed space, where guests pay for a seat at a shared table. Unlike a restaurant, seats are limited and sold in advance, so every dinner has a fixed guest list and a built-in sense of occasion. Most supper clubs run on a set menu, a fixed price per seat, and a host who brings people together around food.

Pick a point of view before you pick recipes. A single cuisine, a seasonal theme, a “everything from my grandmother’s kitchen” story — the concept is what makes people share it. Plan a set menu you can cook confidently for your full guest count, and price the ingredients per head so you know your costs before you set a ticket price.

Your space sets your capacity. A dining table might seat 8; a studio or backyard might do 30. Decide the exact number of seats — this is the number you’ll cap ticket sales at, and a smaller, sold-out table feels far better than a half-empty big one.

Add up your cost per head — ingredients, drinks, rentals, your time — and price above it. Many first-time hosts undercharge; a supper club is an experience, not a cost-plus meal. Consider tiers: an early-bird seat, a regular seat, and a “bring a friend” pair. When you sell tickets on Partiful, free events are always free, and for paid tickets you choose whether to absorb the fee or pass it to guests. See exactly how ticketing fees work.

This is the step that used to mean stitching together an invite, Venmo requests, and a spreadsheet. Now it’s one page. Make a free Partiful event page in under a minute, then turn on paid tickets: set your tiers, cap capacity at your exact seat count, add a promo code for regulars, and let guests pay on the page. Payouts land in your bank via Stripe a few days after the dinner.

Supper clubs grow by word of mouth, not ads. Share your event link in group chats and let the visible guest list do the selling — “who else is going?” is your best marketing. Because millions of people are already on Partiful every month, your dinner can also surface to friends of guests through Explore, so you’re not starting from zero each time.
On the night, check guests in with QR codes at the door — no printed list, no confusion — and give a co-host check-in access if you’ve got a partner working the room.

This is where a supper club stops being an event and becomes a thing people belong to. Create an org profile so guests can follow you and get notified about every future dinner, and re-invite past attendees directly to your next one. The goal isn’t to fill one table — it’s to build a list of people who come back, month after month.

Direct answer: most supper clubs charge somewhere between covering costs and a premium experience price — start by calculating your full cost per head (ingredients, drinks, rentals, space, and your time), then price above it with room for a margin. Tiered pricing helps: an early-bird rate rewards fast RSVPs, a standard rate captures everyone else, and a pair or “bring a friend” tier nudges guests to fill your table for you.

Chasing friends for Venmo, tracking who paid in a spreadsheet, and re-counting seats is the worst part of hosting — and the reason a lot of dinners never become a habit. Selling tickets on a single event page removes all of it: one link, real-time seat counts, payment handled, and a guest list you can actually see. Halloween 2026 lands on a Saturday, which is the best-case scenario for anyone charging admission. You get Friday the 30th and Saturday the 31st as viable party nights, nobody has work the next morning, and demand is at its annual peak. It also means competition for your city’s Saturday night is brutal, so getting tickets live early matters more than usual.

Charging isn’t rude. It’s how you throw a bigger party than your own bank account allows. The costs stack fast: costumes and decor, a fog machine, a DJ or someone’s friend with a controller, a bartender, kegs and mixers, cups, ice, a cleaner for the morning after, maybe a venue or Airbnb.

There’s a second reason, and it’s the one experienced hosts care about: a paid ticket is a commitment device. Free RSVP lists for Halloween routinely see 40–60% no-shows because everyone gets invited to four parties and decides at 9pm. People who paid $20 show up. If you’ve ever bought food and drink for 80 and had 35 walk through the door, you already know why this matters.

Add a paid ticket tier. In ticket setup, enter what you want to receive per ticket and Partiful calculates the guest-facing price, or enter the price you want on the flyer and see what lands in your pocket. Either field works.

Set a capacity limit. Decide the real number your space holds and cap it. A sold-out party is better marketing than an empty one, and a hard cap is what keeps the fire marshal and your landlord out of your night.
Create an early-bird promo code. Discount the first 20–30 tickets. Early sales fund your supply run and, more importantly, put names on a public guest list that makes everyone else want in.

Share it everywhere. Text the link to your group chats, post it to your story, add it to your org profile if you host regularly. Partiful events also surface through Explore and local discovery, so people beyond your contacts can find it.

Run the door with QR check-in. Scan tickets from your phone on the night. You can give check-in permissions to someone who isn’t a host, such as a friend on door duty or hired staff, so you’re not the bottleneck at 11pm.
Early bird: first 25 tickets at a discount. Creates urgency in week one and gets your guest list visibly populated.
At the door: priced $5–10 above GA. Rewards the people who committed and covers the chaos premium.
Costume required / costume discount: a fun one. Some hosts run a lower tier for anyone who commits to a costume in the questionnaire field.
Free tier for the crew: the people helping set up, bartend, or DJ get comped. Free tickets carry no fees, so this costs you nothing.
Keep it to two or three tiers. More than that and people stall on the decision.
A paid event page needs more information than a free one, because people are deciding whether to spend money on a night out:
What the ticket includes: open bar? BYOB? One drink? Say it plainly. This is the single biggest source of door-night arguments.
Costume expectations: required, encouraged, or themed. “Costume required, no exceptions” is a legitimate door policy and people respect it if you say it up front.
Start and end time: real ones. “10pm–3am” tells people when to pre-game.
Address handling: many hosts keep the exact address hidden until purchase, then send it by text blast the day of.
Age policy: if it’s 21+, say so before someone buys.

To maintain this environment, we have established the following Community Guidelines, which apply to all users across our platforms. By using Partiful, you agree to abide by these guidelines and our Terms of Service. Violations of these guidelines may result in deleted content or events, disabling or banning accounts, or other restrictions.
Harassment: Do not engage in any form of harassment, including bullying, sexual harassment or blackmail.
Physical Threats: Do not threaten to harm an individual or group of people. Credible threats or incitement of violence will be removed from the platform.
Privacy: Respect the privacy of others. Do not share personally identifiable information (PII) without consent, or engage in doxxing activities.
Hate Speech: Hate speech or any form of hateful conduct is not tolerated. This includes the promotion of violence or discrimination based on protected characteristics.
Violent Extremism: Do not organize, promote, or support violent extremism or terrorist activities in any form.

Child Safety: Protect the safety of minors by refraining from sharing or soliciting sexually explicit content involving individuals under the age of 18. Any content that sexualizes children is strictly prohibited.
Sexual Harassment: Do not share, distribute, or create sexually explicit or sexually suggestive content of other people without the subject’s consent.
Self-Harm and Suicide: Do not glorify, promote, or encourage self-harm, suicide, or other harmful behaviors. This includes content that depicts or normalizes such actions.
Spam and Platform Manipulation: Do not engage in spamming activities or manipulate engagement metrics. This includes the use of spambots, self-bots, or any other artificial means to inflate activity.
Security and Fraud: Protect the security of our platform and users. Refrain from engaging in activities that compromise data security, promote scams, or perpetrate fraud.

Misinformation: Content that is false, misleading, and can lead to significant risk of physical or societal harm may not be shared on Partiful. We may remove content if we reasonably believe its spread could result in damage to physical infrastructure, injury of others, obstruction of participation in civic processes, or the endangerment of public health. Misrepresentation of identity and deceptive practices are also prohibited.
Intellectual Property Rights: Respect intellectual property rights and do not share content that violates copyright or other rights.
Illegal Activities: Do not engage in or promote any illegal activities, including human trafficking, sexual solicitation, or any other criminal behavior.
Regulated Goods and Activities: Do not promote or facilitate the sale of regulated or dangerous goods, illegal gambling, or any other unlawful activities.

If you encounter content or activities that violate these guidelines or our Terms of Service, please report them to us promptly at hello@partiful.com. We rely on our community to help maintain a safe and welcoming environment for all users. Thank you for your cooperation in upholding these standards.

/about.description: We're a team of party people who think it should be easier to plan events. With Partiful, you can create invitations, track RSVPs, sell tickets, and bring people together in a way that's fun and effortless.
h1: From “we should hang out” to “last night was a movie”
Built for the way people actually gather today
p: Since the beginning, we’ve found excuses to come together — around fires, at feasts, in clubs, in backyards. Gathering is one of the most human things we do.

But somewhere along the way, it got complicated. A dozen apps, three group chats, and a scheduling miracle just to get friends in the same room. We’ve never had more ways to connect, yet somehow, hanging out feels harder than ever.

That’s where Partiful comes in. We make it easy to go from idea, to invite, to actual memories. Whether you’re hosting a gathering or looking to join one, getting together should feel fun — not like a second job.
Partiful is the home for every kind of night you’ll want to remember: the milestone parties, the casual hangouts, the nights-in that accidentally turn into nights-on-the-town.
We’ve designed Partiful to take the work out of planning so you can focus on the fun. Send invites without wrangling a group chat. RSVP with just your name and number. Discover where the fun is.

Because when it’s easier to get together, you do it more often. And the truth is — life isn’t about being “connected.” It’s about being in the same room, laughing at the same stupid joke, making the kind of nights you’ll talk about for years.

We’re a small team who cares a little too much about getting people together. One of us will cook all day just to host the perfect dinner. Another can’t resist a warehouse rave. Someone else thinks planning an over-the-top birthday is a form of self-care, while another is happiest tucked in the corner of a house party talking to the same two people all night long.
Different vibes, same belief: gathering is what gives life meaning. That’s why we’re building Partiful — to make getting together easier, so more of those moments actually happen.
